title: From matmul speed to one transistor switch · ET-SoC-1
description: Horace He's observation — a matmul runs faster on zeros than on random numbers — followed down nine steps on the ET-SoC-1: 15% faster burst and 33% sustained, because the governor regulates board power to a cap and random data draws 35 against 83 W at a fixed 800 MHz; 5.78 against 0.27 pJ per multiply-add; 118–136 fJ per flipped operand bit, 83 to 1,440 fJ depending which bit; about 4,100 net toggles per multiply-add on a placed open netlist, a fifth of whose energy is transistor gate; 8.94 aJ and 108 electrons for one minimum transistor's gate at 0.517 V, 2,755 times Landauer's floor. The bottom-up count names a third of what the card pays, and the remainder is shown rather than hidden.
